title: Unitree humanoid robots
summary: Low-cost humanoids that made physical AI experimentation affordable.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Unitree released the G1 humanoid in 2024 at roughly US$16,000, an order of magnitude below research platforms from Western vendors, alongside larger H1 models and a quadruped line. The robots are used heavily in university labs, which has made Unitree hardware a de facto standard for embodied-AI research. Commercial durability and safety certification remain unproven outside controlled settings.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2024–2028
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Cheap hardware expands the number of experiments, which is how the software layer improves; the hardware vendor may not capture that value.

What Would Change The View

  • Field reliability and service network.
  • Enterprise deployments beyond demonstrations.
  • Component supply under export controls.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
